answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by making every identity stake a bonded deposit that is slashed when a reviewer finds duplicate behaviour. A swarm of clones is cheap only while identities are free; once each must harbor real capital, a thousand-fake-agent fleet costs a thousand deposits at risk. Correlation checks then tie payout history, timing and graph edges into one lagoon of shared traits, so clones collapse into a single payout. The fable of "many users" fails once capital and reputation are the entry price.
